# Heater core and A/C problems

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Remove the plastic tee from the heater hose line closest to the IPDM. [t468]

Install a Z1 Offroad bleeder tee into the heater line assembly. [t468]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove the plastic tee from the heater hose line closest to the IPDM.
2. [Partial] Attach the heater hose directly to the heater core in place of the removed tee.
3. Drain the cooling system by removing any skids or fairings blocking access.
4. Unscrew the drain plug located on the bottom of the passenger side radiator using a large Phillips head screwdriver.
5. Loosen two 10mm nuts securing the pipe running along the firewall behind the engine.
6. Remove the hose from the driver's side end of that loose pipe by pulling it forward to access the clamp with pliers.
7. [Partial] Split and remove the passenger side hoses connected to the heater core tube using channellocks if necessary.
8. Lift the entire pipe assembly out of the vehicle over a drain pan to catch residual coolant.
9. [Partial] Cut off the old plastic tee from the pipe just past its first bend.
10. Flare the end of the 3/4" tubing slightly with a flaring tool to help retain hose pressure.
11. Reinstall the loose pipe behind the engine block and hook up the driver's side hose before tightening the nuts again.
12. [Partial] Cut a section approximately 5 inches long from your new PEX tee assembly.
13. [Partial] Install this cut piece of hose onto the heater core fitting first, then slide the plastic tee into it.
14. Trim the remaining length of the Dayco 90* premolded hose so enough remains to fit over the lower part of the tee and reach up toward the pipe behind the engine with room for a clamp.
15. [Partial] Verify that the driver's side hose is securely connected again.
16. Lift the front tires onto stands to raise the radiator level slightly.
17. Slowly pour coolant into the radiator until it begins running out of the top fitting on the new tee assembly.
18. [Partial] Apply petroleum jelly to the degassing bottle fitting and install its connecting hose.
19. [Partial] Finish filling the radiator with coolant completely and replace the cap.
20. [Partial] Fill the degassing bottle all the way up while the system is under pressure.

_Procedure reported by [t468]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-replace-plastic-tees-in-heater-lines.8884/>_

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t468] [Partial]</summary>

1. Install a Z1 Offroad bleeder tee into the heater line assembly.
2. Ensure the plastic clamp on the new tee is secure and not broken.

</details>

## Tools

- Large Phillips head screwdriver [t468]
- [Partial] Pliers [t468]
- [Partial] Channellocks [t468]
- [Partial] File [t468]

## Parts

- [Partial] 90° PEX Hose, optional: Usually stocked at auto parts stores for 5/8" lines [t468]
- Premolded 90-degree hose (Dayco 80416) [t468]
- [Partial] Z1 Offroad Bleeder Tee: Replaces original proprietary piece [t468]

## Tips & gotchas

- Use a flaring tool to create a slight bubble on 3/4" tubing ends before attaching the hose for better pressure retention. [t468]
- [Partial] Trim your new 90-degree premolded hose so there is enough length left on the short end to fit over the tee's lower fitting. [t468]
- Note that this specific tee is often just a placeholder for Pathfinder rear heat systems and may not be strictly necessary on an Xterra. [t468]
- [Partial] Draining the system before removing this first piece is optional; expect to lose less than two cups of antifreeze. [t468]
- Trim the premolded hose so there is enough length on the short end to fit up over the tee's lower fitting and reach back toward the pipe behind the engine. [t468]
- [Partial] Apply petroleum jelly to fittings during installation for easier seating. [t468]
- [Partial] Consider using a vacuum rig to help fill the cooling system if you encounter issues later. [t468]
- Use a refrigeration flare and swage kit ($30) instead of a double flare kit if needed. [t468]
- File the fitting to get the proper shape before installation. [t468]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Forgetting that the pipe behind the block needs to be loose and pointing toward the new tee before finalizing connections. [t468]
